messages:
incident-bot: Pager: prefix-cache error-rate and mem-pressure spike in prod-east-2 (kv-store). Alerts: 5xx increase, request latency > 2s for /v1/generate endpoints. Auto-page to oncall group.

oncall-alex: saw it. hitting the dashboard now, memory on kv-nodes at 92% and continuing to climb. continuous-batching queue depth up ~6x. tagging @eng-runtime and @eng-ml.

eng-runtime-leah: jumping in. any obvious recent deploys?

oncall-alex: no infra deploys in last 30m. small model push 12m ago (embedding-model v2.3) — not obvious.

eng-ml-omar: model push was just an embedding change; unrelated to generation paths normally but will check prompt/tokenizer changes in model packaging.

eng-sre-marta: logs show a lot of "prefix_key:*" keys being created; cardinality spike — looks like prefix hashing changed and many keys aren't being deduped.

sre-ravi: confirmed. KV write rate jumped from ~4k/s to ~60k/s. Bloom filter miss rate also spiked. This looks like cache blowup (hot keyspace explosion).

eng-runtime-leah: if prefix hash changed and created unique keys per request, continuous-batching will happily create cache entries for each prompt prefix. until TTL eviction catches up, memory balloons. we need immediate mitigation: throttle cache writes and revert batching aggressiveness.

oncall-alex: agreed. attempting quick mitigation: reducing continuous-batcher max_concurrency from 32 -> 8 in prod-east-2 for service-realtime. running:
```bash
curl -XPOST https://control-plane.internal/configs/service-realtime -d '{"continuous_batcher.max_concurrency":8}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN'
```

incident-bot: Deploybot: config update queued on prod-east-2, change id cfg-911 triggered by oncall-alex.

eng-runtime-leah: also enabling write-through disable flag for prefix cache to avoid heavy writes:
```bash
curl -XPOST https://control-plane.internal/flags -d '{"prefix_cache.write_enabled":false}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN'
```

sre-ravi: applying throttle now and evicting the largest prefix shards. running an eviction sweep for keys matching pref:prompt:* with safe-delete.

eng-ml-omar: quick check on model packaging: tokenizer upgrade was rolled into embedding-model v2.3 and also picked up by a downstream template normalization job. it changed normalization for whitespace and quotes -> will change prompt string before hashing. that could produce lots of distinct hashes.

customer-success-jane: any customer impact? I’m seeing increased error reports from three enterprise customers on east region (timeouts). Need ETA to share.

oncall-alex: ETA depends on eviction and cache TTLs — after throttle + disable writes we should see memory usage stabilize in ~8-12 minutes, errors should drop. telling customers we have a mitigation in flight.

eng-sre-marta: eviction sweep completed for largest 50k keys. mem usage dropped to 78% from 92% and KV write rate is down to ~7k/s. latency improving.

incident-bot: Incident: prefix-cache-collision-1964123456 created. Severity: Sev2. Impact: increased 5xx and latency for generation endpoints in prod-east-2.

eng-runtime-leah: long-term fix: revert tokenizer/normalizer changes in the prompt hashing pipeline or add a normalization compatibility layer so previous hashes remain stable. short-term: patch hashing to include model_version tag so different tokenizers don't mix keys.

eng-ml-omar: can confirm tokenizer normalization diff is the root cause. I have a patch that 1) maps new normalization to legacy canonical form for hashing, and 2) adds a model_version suffix to cache key. Patch ready for canary.

oncall-alex: do we want to roll patch to canary in prod-east-2 now?

eng-runtime-leah: yes. but we need a controlled rollout with traffic routing and canary telemetry. schedule 10% traffic to patched runtime for 15m, watch cache-key cardinality and mem.

eng-ml-omar: deploying canary now. canary id can-1964. routeset updated to send 10% of new sessions to canary.

incident-bot: Canary can-1964 deployed. Telemetry: enabled prefix-key-cardinality, cache-write-rate, kv-mem-usage.

sre-ravi: initial canary metrics look good: canary nodes show proper dedupe, key creation rate 2.1k/s vs 18k/s on unpatched. no error increase.

customer-success-jane: passing to PM and ops to draft customer note: brief description + mitigation + ETA for permanent fix and rollback options.

eng-sre-marta: recommendation: keep write_disable flag on for 30m after full rollout to ensure the backlog is cleared then re-enable writes. Also increase TTL on existing prefix keys from 1h -> 15m to accelerate reclamation. running TTL bump now.

oncall-alex: TTL bump applied. mem usage now 64%. error rate back to baseline over last 7m. Thanks team.

eng-runtime-leah: plan for next steps: 1) promote patch to 100% with staged traffic shift 25/50/100 over 40m, 2) cleanup keyspace, 3) postmortem writeup and follow-up action items (testing for tokenizer-propagation, add regression test in model onboarding).

eng-ml-omar: I'll prepare a model-onboarding checklist update to ensure tokenizer changes are flagged and hashing compatibility is enforced.

customer-success-jane: I emailed affected customers with a short note and ETA for full resolution. will follow up with individualized context if requested.

eng-sre-marta: handing off to night oncall. @oncall-alex handing to @oncall-kim in 25 minutes. All mitigations in place, canary healthy.

oncall-alex: handing off. summary: prefix cache key cardinality spike due to tokenizer normalization change in model pipeline -> cache blowup -> continuous-batcher amplification. Immediate mitigations applied: reduced batcher concurrency, disabled prefix-cache writes, eviction sweep, TTL bump, canary deploy of hashing-compat patch. System stable.

eng-runtime-leah: leaving some runbook notes in the incident doc. please escalate if any re-regression.

incident-bot: Incident annotated: handoff to oncall-kim scheduled at 1964125289.

oncall-alex: thanks all :thumbsup:.

eng-ml-omar: follow-up tasks will include: regression test for prompt-hash, adding a canary check comparing pre/post tokenizer outputs, and adding an alert for sudden cache-key cardinality increases beyond X% baseline.

eng-sre-marta: tagging this for a full postmortem. assigning owners: runtime -> leah, ML -> omar, SRE -> ravi.

customer-success-jane: I'll track customer comms thread and post updates.

eng-runtime-leah: noting a minor action: add feature-flag to allow prefixed key namespace isolation per model version to avoid cross-version pollution.

oncall-alex: logging handoff and closing this active pager.
